html:
Command palette and desktop invocation

Press Ctrl+K on Windows/Linux or Cmd+K on macOS in the desktop Agent UI. The More menu also contains Command palette. The dialog contains the existing composer, attachments and controls, so a draft follows you between the two views. Escape dismisses the palette and restores focus. Dismissal does not stop a task.

Start input with / to search registered application commands. Arrow keys select, Tab completes, and Enter executes through the existing command control plane. Unavailable commands show their reason. Unknown commands stay command errors. Opening, filtering and executing commands make no model calls. Empty input shows safe available commands, with recently used safe commands first for this page.

Plain text uses the normal Agent submission operation, payload, task queue, attachments, capability selection and permission policies. No classifier, prompt wrapper or extra model call is added. Enter submits; Shift+Enter inserts a newline. The palette is a UI surface and has no Agent skill or model-visible tools.

Conversations and Gateways

An in-app invocation uses the exact visible conversation by default. The header shows its identity and the command run identity. Change conversation opens the existing conversation navigator; choose a conversation and reopen the palette. New conversation uses normal new-chat defaults. The launcher starts with New conversation, ignoring saved conversations and global current-run restoration. An explicit conversation parameter on a palette URL selects that exact conversation. Missing or deleted selections are not replaced with another conversation.

Target shows the canonical ordered Gateway selection. Change target opens the existing multi-Gateway selector. Controls retain the saved conversation target, including remote Gateways and unavailable targets. Admission captures a copy of the selection; subsequent edits affect future tasks. Task target identifies captured scope when it is available. No second registry or selector is maintained.

Command availability and backend validation still bind exact conversation, request and run IDs. If that scope changes while the palette is open, reopen it to review the new scope before executing. Deletion opens the existing confirmation dialog.

Progress, interactions and accessibility

Submitting is a transport state. Queued, processing, waiting, completed, stopped and failed states come from the existing durable task lane and per-turn state. The palette adds no polling loop or SSE connection. A bounded excerpt uses the same final response as the conversation. Open conversation navigates to the observed task so you can answer questions, review unsafe-action approval or use full task controls. Slash stop/pause/resume use their normal exact-scope controls. No approval is granted by opening or dismissing the palette.

The native modal dialog contains keyboard focus, labels the conversation/targets, uses the shared command listbox and announces status. Escape restores the invoking focus. Layout fits narrow desktop-browser viewports without horizontal overflow; the separately served phone UI keeps its existing composer and slash commands. There are no palette animations or percentage estimates.

Desktop launcher support

With the runtime already running and aor on PATH:

aor palette
aor palette --url https://your-runtime.example

The default URL uses configured server host/port, translating a wildcard bind host to loopback. --url accepts an HTTP(S) runtime base URL without credentials, query or fragment. It opens /agent-ui?palette=1&ui=desktop in the system browser and exits. Browser policy determines whether a window is reused or a new tab opens; reliably focusing an existing tab requires a resident browser/native integration. The launcher does not start a second runtime.

Platform System-wide invocation Verification
Linux X11 Bind aor palette in the desktop custom shortcut manager CLI/browser boundary tested on Linux; real desktop registration is user configured
Linux Wayland Bind the same command through GNOME/KDE or the compositor's shortcut manager No universal Wayland registrar claimed; compositor binding not live-tested
Windows Bind the installed command through an OS shortcut or launcher Portable browser-launch contract tested with a fake browser; native OS launch unverified
macOS Bind the installed command through Shortcuts/Automator or a launcher Portable browser-launch contract tested with a fake browser; native OS launch unverified

For a Python environment installation, use its absolute executable path in the OS shortcut, for example /path/to/smto/.venv/bin/aor palette. Choose an unused OS shortcut and enable/disable it in the OS shortcut manager. Conflicts and reserved bindings at that layer belong to the OS. No resident native global registrar is included in this browser-based product.

Invocation settings inside the palette configure the in-app binding, enablement and current/new conversation behavior for this tab using existing session settings. Changes apply immediately. Modifier-only and known browser/app conflicts are rejected. Browsers may consume additional keys; use the More menu to choose another binding. No OS shortcut is seized automatically.

Privacy and troubleshooting

The launcher has no keyboard event stream or background hook. It reads neither clipboard, screen nor active-window content. The browser only handles key events inside its focused document. Prompt persistence remains the existing composer draft policy; no palette history database or prompt diagnostics are added.

If no browser opens, configure the default browser or visit the palette URL directly. If the runtime is unavailable, start it or correct --url. If a shortcut conflicts, use the palette button, another in-app binding or the OS shortcut manager. If target or conversation settings are unavailable, fix them using the existing Controls. Canonical backend/network errors retain their Error IDs and remediation.

Source owners: command_palette.js moves the existing dock and projects state; app.js owns the single submitComposer handler and lifecycle hooks; slash_commands.js, command_protocol.js and command_actions.js remain shared; prompt_queue.js provides exact-task observation; api/cli.py owns aor palette.
